relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with Alexander disease and a GFAP variant: "Molecular analysis confirmed a missense mutation in the GFAP gene."
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON. One in-scope person, the single unnamed patient of a case report (label 'patient'); the 31-year-old mother is mentioned only as the referred pregnant woman with no testing or features, so she gets no row. The variant is printed only as '73Met<Thr' (the Markdown shows '<', i.e. '<', where '>' was likely intended); no cDNA, transcript, zygosity or parental testing is printed. The protein string is recorded in both variant_original_string and protein_hgvs_as_stated although it lacks a 'p.' prefix. 'previously reported 1' refers to the mutation (ref 1), not to the patient, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is left null. The statement that the mutation is de novo 'in most cases' is general and is not used for this patient. Publication year is not printed as such (only 'Received March 25, 2008'), so year is null. Age at onset is gestational (32 weeks' gestation), so its ISO field is null; age at diagnosis is taken as the 2-day neonatal MRI where AD was 'strongly suggested' (time of the molecular confirmation not given). The 2-month MRI sentence is broken across a page boundary ('small cav-' ... 'itations in the frontal white matter'); the cavitations are not recorded because the spans would have to be joined. 'Questionable abnormal white matter' at 33 weeks is hedged and not recorded as a separate feature. 'Normal birth parameters' is a normal measurement set as a whole and is recorded as such ('abnormal birth parameters' excluded) without excluding anything more specific. 'Accelerated head growth' is recorded as a feature but not as checklist macrocephaly, since head size relative to norms is not stated. The neonatal MRI 'fulfilled all the diagnostic MR imaging criteria', but the criteria are not listed in this paper, so nothing further was inferred. Discussion statements about the neonatal variant in general (seizures, etc.) are not applied to this patient. No internal contradictions found.
